explain_verdicts.V97 idx_orders_paid_at: KEEP. Index Scan idx_orders_paid_at chosen by the DEFAULT planner for the current 30d window (1.9 ms), previous window (0.9 ms), oldest monthly bucket (0.9 ms) and current partial month (0.4 ms). With bound parameters (what Hibernate/pgjdbc send) after 6 executions plan_cache_mode=auto still uses it. Without the index: Parallel Seq Scan, 21.5 ms (window) and 40.4 ms (month). Whole 14-statement revenue load of one cache miss: 27.7 ms with, 151.7-176.3 ms without (about 6x) at 100k orders, growing linearly with the table.
explain_verdicts.V97 worst case: plan_cache_mode=force_generic_plan (not the default) cannot prove the partial predicate for a parameter and falls back to Bitmap Heap Scan on idx_orders_status_created, 11.3 ms: acceptable, no action.
explain_verdicts.question bank counts by status/section/p: Seq Scan + HashAggregate, 14.3 ms for 40k rows (inherent: every shared non-deleted question is counted; the forced visibility index is slower at 15.7 ms). One pass replaces the two legacy grouped queries (7.9 + 9.9 ms).
explain_verdicts.question bank created in window: Seq Scan 7.4 ms (no created_at index; forced index not faster). Fine at expected volumes.

production_concerns.finding: The 12-month series issues one grouped statement per month (12) plus one per window (2) = 14 statements per uncached revenue build (Hibernate statistics: 12 statements for the series, 0 entity loads). With V97 each is about 1 ms (27.7 ms total at 100k orders); the section is cached 60 s.
production_concerns.suggested_fix: None needed now. If the orders table grows by orders of magnitude, a single grouped statement by month would remove the 12 round trips but needs a database-specific date_trunc/zone function, which the portable-JPQL constraint of the phase rules out.

production_concerns.finding: Both are sequential scans (14.3 ms and 7.4 ms at 40k questions); no index can avoid reading every shared question for the counts. Linear growth.
production_concerns.suggested_fix: Nothing now. If the bank passes ~1M rows add questions(created_at) WHERE deleted = false for the created-in-window count.

production_concerns.finding: BigDecimal amounts are serialized as JSON numbers (verified: jsonPath numeric match 1500000.5), so a JavaScript client parses them as double. That is exact up to 2^53 (~9e15) and loses trailing-zero scale (1500000.50 arrives as 1500000.5); fine for VND/USD display, but the client must format with the currency's fraction digits and must never sum across currencies.
production_concerns.suggested_fix: Phase 5: type the amount fields as number, format via Intl.NumberFormat with the row's currency, no cross-currency totals.

observations: No production bug found in Phase 4 code; every success criterion in the phase file was met (overview/billing/itembank group, architecture diff, MockMvc/JWT ACADEMIC_MANAGER question bank OK + revenue FORBIDDEN, PLATFORM_ADMIN revenue OK, Postgres-gated migration test with the same command as Phase 3, EXPLAIN recorded).
V97 was added 'judgment-based' by the cook; the EXPLAIN evidence now supports it: default planner uses it for all four revenue query shapes and the load is about 6x faster at 100k orders. Keep it.

The question bank section for academic callers is computed and cached once per bucket: the admin bucket has its own questionBank entry, so the same payload is cached twice (one entry per bucket). That is by design of the visibility-bucket cache and costs one extra small query every 60 s.

Real policy outcome (derived, not assumed): PLATFORM_MANAGER sees all 10 sections exactly like PLATFORM_ADMIN and shares its cache bucket; ACADEMIC_MANAGER, ACADEMIC_STAFF and legacy PLATFORM_AUTHOR see only questionBank (bucket 'questionBank'); a platform role that also carries a tenant id, tenant roles, role-less and null callers see nothing (bucket 'none').

The status list guard in BillingRevenueOverviewQueriesTest documents that the order lifecycle has no FAILED or refunded status (PENDING, PAID, CANCELLED, EXPIRED only), so PAID-only is the complete revenue rule today; adding a refund status will fail that guard and force a decision.
The Visibility enum has a single value (SHARED); 'non-shared questions are excluded' is therefore vacuous today. A guard test fails if a second visibility is added.
AdminDashboardControllerTest.assertNoFacadeWasTouched previously ignored the tenancyOverview, revenue and itembank facades; it now includes them (stricter, not weaker).
